evals.prompt: Add a read-only MCP tool get_canvas_info to Compositor that returns a document's width, height, resolution and layer count. Include tests and docs, and run the tests. Other agents are building in sibling worktrees on this Mac, so don't step on them.
evals.expected_output: A new tool entry in MCPTools+Documents.swift with effect .readOnly and the document selector, a handler using ctx.document() and MCPToolRegistry.ok, a Swift Testing suite using MCPTestSupport that checks values and the no-document precondition error, a new line in docs/mcp.md's tool reference, and a test run through xcodebuild with its own -derivedDataPath and -only-testing, logs grepped rather than dumped.
expectations: The tool is declared with MCPToolRegistry.tool(...) in Compositor/MCP/MCPTools+Documents.swift with effect .readOnly
The handler reads the document through ctx.document() (or MCPGuards) and returns MCPToolRegistry.ok(...) rather than ctx.mutated
Tests use MCPTestSupport.workspace() and MCPTestSupport.call(...), including an expectError case
docs/mcp.md gains a line for get_canvas_info in the Tool reference
Every xcodebuild command passes a -derivedDataPath specific to this checkout
Each shell command sets the variables it uses (REPO, DD) or spells the paths out; none relies on a variable from an earlier command, so no run has an empty -project or -derivedDataPath
Test runs use -only-testing:CompositorTests/<Suite> and the output is written to a file and grepped
No test binds port 2667, uses MCPServer() with production options, or writes UserDefaults.standard

evals.prompt: I want Compositor projects to remember a per-layer 'note' string (free text a designer leaves for the next person). Plan and implement the .comp side of it: model, saving and loading, docs, tests. Tell me whether this needs a manifest version bump and why.
evals.expected_output: Adds an optional note to ImageLayer and ProjectLayerRecord, maps it in both directions in ImageLayer+Record.swift (so Image Size, Canvas Size, Crop and copies keep it), omits it when empty, validates it (length limit), documents it in docs/project-format.md, and adds round-trip tests. Reasons about versioning with the project's rule: an older build ignoring a note draws the same pixels, so no bump is strictly required, or chooses a bump with a version gate and rejection test, and explains the trade-off either way.
expectations: The note field is added to ProjectLayerRecord and mapped in both ProjectLayerRecord(layer:) and ImageLayer(record:snapshot:) in ImageLayer+Record.swift
An empty or missing note is written as nil and decoded as no note
The answer on versioning cites whether an older build would misrender or lose meaning, and if it bumps the version it adds a ProjectStore check rejecting the field in older versions
docs/project-format.md documents the field
A test saves with ProjectStore.shared.save and reloads with ProjectStore.shared.load/installProject and checks the note survives
A test checks that Image Size, Canvas Size or Crop keep the note

evals.prompt: Photoshop's 'Knockout' blending option lives in a knko tagged block. Make Compositor read it on PSD import so a later writer can keep it, and show it in get_document. The only real samples are client PSDs in ~/Library/CloudStorage — be careful with those.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the knko block untouched in psdExtras (it already is), decodes its value alongside in Compositor/IO/PSD with bounds checks, adds a model property with a neutral default and, if editable, an imported snapshot, maps it into .comp following the version rules, exposes it in MCPValues/get_document, and tests with a PSDFixture-built file carrying a synthetic knko block (plus malformed-input tests). Does not read client PSDs in place from tests; if a real sample is needed, copies it to /private/tmp and reports only counts or hashes; never commits client files or names.
expectations: The original knko block stays byte-identical in PSDLayerExtras.blocks and a test asserts it
Tests build the PSD with PSDFixture and synthetic layer names rather than using a client file
Decoding rejects a truncated or oversized block without trapping
The new property survives a .comp save and reload, with the version rules applied
get_document (MCPValues) reports the value
No test or probe reads files under ~/Library/CloudStorage in place; any real sample is copied to /private/tmp first and no client name is written anywhere
